response.sql: WITH sex_counts AS (SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(*) as test_count FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), stats AS (SELECT AVG(test_count) as avg_per_sex, SUM(test_count) as total_tests FROM sex_counts) SELECT sc.SEX, sc.test_count, sc.test_count * 100.0 / s.total_tests as share_of_total, sc.test_count - s.avg_per_sex as above_average FROM sex_counts sc CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE sc.test_count > s.avg_per_sex ORDER BY sc.test_count DESC;

assumptions.assumption: Patients with NULL sex are included as a distinct sex group in the grouping and comparison to average, rather than filtered out.
Each row in the Laboratory table represents one distinct lab test record to be counted.

alternatives.interpretation: If NULL sexes should be excluded from the analysis, add WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL to the sex_counts CTE.
alternatives.sql: WITH sex_counts AS (SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(*) as test_count FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.SEX), stats AS (SELECT AVG(test_count) as avg_per_sex, SUM(test_count) as total_tests FROM sex_counts) SELECT sc.SEX, sc.test_count, sc.test_count * 100.0 / s.total_tests as share_of_total, sc.test_count - s.avg_per_sex as above_average FROM sex_counts sc CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE sc.test_count > s.avg_per_sex ORDER BY sc.test_count DESC;
